Example Instructional Routine:

In the story, Sheep is described as looking very plain. 
If something is plain, it is very simple in style, with no pattern or decoration.
Say the word with me…… plain!
A bedroom with white walls, no posters and no decoration could be described as plain. A cupcake with no fillings or icing is plain.

texts: Sheep was described as being plain
That means Sheep does not look fancy or flashy. Sheep looks simple compared to others.

If something is plain, does it have lots of decorations?
Does plain mean not as good?

A narrative is a story. We tell stories with characters, events and a problem that is solved.

Who is our story about?
 
We call this the character.

The characters find a way to solve the problem.

Bear, Lion, Moose, Zebra and Sheep

Bear is very cranky and the other animals are scared.
Look at pages 7-21 of the text.
Sheep makes Bear a soft pillow to help him sleep.

In this lesson, you will need:
Bears are large animals that live in many parts of the world. They are strong, furry creatures with sharp claws and teeth. Bears have excellent noses that can detect food from a great distance.
Image credit: Google slides stock image
Why do you think bears hibernate in winter instead of staying awake?
Most bears like to live in forests, mountains, or near rivers. They make their homes in caves, hollow trees, or dens. A den is a safe, quiet place where a bear can rest and sleep.
Image credit: Google slides stock image

Bears eat many different foods. They are called omnivores because they eat plants and meat. Some bears like to eat berries, nuts, roots, and honey. They can also catch fish in rivers or eat small animals.
Image credit: Google slides stock image

When winter comes, many bears hibernate. This means they spend a very long time sleeping in their den. During hibernation, a bear’s body slows down, and it lives off the fat it stored from eating lots of food before winter. If someone were to wake a bear up during hibernation, the bear might feel cranky.
Image credit: Google slides stock image

Even though bears are big and sometimes grumpy, they are also very clever. They can climb trees, swim across rivers, and walk long distances. Bears need quiet, safe spaces to live. People should not approach wild bears too closely, as they may feel scared or bothered.
Image credit: Google slides stock image
Bears are important animals in nature. They help keep forests and rivers healthy. In stories, bears are often shown as strong or sometimes cranky, but they can also be gentle and caring.
Image credit: Google slides stock image
Why do you think bears hibernate in winter instead of staying awake?

Example Instructional Routine:

In the story, Moose’s antlers are described as marvellous.
If something is marvellous, it is wonderful or exciting.
Say the word with me…… marvellous!
Seeing a rainbow after the rain is marvellous. Seeing a shooting star in the night sky is marvellous.

texts: Marvellous means extremely wonderful or impressive
Image credit: Google slides stock image
That tells us the antlers are not just big. They are so impressive and wonderful that they make others stop and stare.
What would be a marvellous present you’d like to receive?
Describe this picture using the word marvellous
The fireworks were marvellous to watch.
Image credit: Google slides stock image
The party was marvellous because surprises kept appearing all night.
Which of these words are similar to marvellous?

and the problem

Use the pictures to help you think of ideas.
Label your drawing with a word to name or describe your character.

In this lesson, you will need:
Why do you think animals like to live in caves instead of outside?
Image credit: Google slides stock image

A cave is a big, hollow space found inside a hill or mountain. Some caves are small, while others are so big you could fit houses inside. Caves can be dark, cool, and sometimes a little scary if you go inside without a light.
Image credit: Google slides stock image

Caves are made in different ways. Some are shaped by water that slowly wears away rock. Others are formed when lava from a volcano hardens and leaves a tunnel behind. Over many years, caves can become full of interesting shapes, such as pointy icicle-shaped rocks called stalactites that hang from the ceiling.
Image credit: Google slides stock image

Many animals like to live in caves because they are safe and quiet. Bats hang upside down in caves to sleep. Bears use caves as dens, especially when they hibernate in winter. Lions, wolves and even some insects may also hide in caves. A cave can protect animals from the rain, wind, and hot sun.
Image credit: Google slides stock image

People sometimes explore caves, too. Explorers need special equipment like helmets and torches to see where they are going. Some caves have drawings made by people long ago, telling us stories about how they lived.
Image credit: Google slides stock image

Caves can feel frightening because you never know what might be inside. They are dark, echoey, and sometimes a little damp. But caves are also wonderful natural homes that give shelter to many animals.
Image credit: Google slides stock image
If something is described as a bore, it is dull and uninteresting.
19. Lesson Slides Extended Daily lesson.notes:

Example Instructional Routine:

In the text, Lion described the Moose’s antlers as a bore.
If something is described as a bore, it is dull and uninteresting.
Say the word with me…… bore!
Waiting in a very long line can be a bore. Being stuck inside on a rainy day can be a bore.

texts:
Watching paint dry could be described as a 
bore because…
it is slow and not exciting.
it is loud and full of action.

Which of these activities would you describe
as a bore?
Image credit: Google slides stock image
Why might you describe a movie as a bore?

It is too long
Nothing exciting happens.
It is similar to another movie.
Image credit: Google slides stock image
When the weekend feels like a bore, I ask my family to ____________________
Image credit: Google slides stock image
Draw a picture of something that feels like a bore
Image credit: Google slides stock image
We use question words when asking a question
Asking questions about The Very Cranky Bear
What were his friends trying to do in the cave?
Asking questions about The Very Cranky Bear
On a cold and rainy day.
Asking questions about The Very Cranky Bear

Why did the friends go into the
cave?
She made him a pillow to sleep on.
Today we are going to focus on the question word ‘how’
‘How’ asks us to tell the way something happens. It makes us think about the actions, the feelings, or the process.
How do you feel when you play with your friends?
How do you spend time with your family?
How do you feel when somebody leaves you out of their game?
Answer these how questions from The Very Cranky Bear
Which question word tells us the way that something happens?
Turn to the page titled: Lesson 3: Sentence-level writing
Use the think aloud to help you with your questions.

Choose one moment from the story and create two different 
‘how’ questions about the same moment.

Example Instructional Routine:

In the story, Sheep feels worried because Bear is angry and loud, and the other animals’ ideas are not helping. Each time they try to cheer the bear up, he gets crankier instead of calmer. At one point, Sheep is worried that Bear has eaten up the other animals.
If you feel worried, you feel anxious about a problem or about something that might happen.
Say the word with me…… worried!
You might feel worried before a big performance. You might feel worried on your first day at school.

texts: Turn to pages 7 & 8 of the text

How do the illustrations help us to understand what is going on in the story?
23. Lesson Slides Extended Daily lesson.notes:
Before reading-
Activate prior knowledge
What can illustrations show that words sometimes don’t tell us?
Have you noticed anything special that Grace wears or draws in the pictures? What do you think those little details might tell us about her?
Have students make personal connections
Do you have objects or symbols (e.g., jewellery, art, decorations, clothing) that show something important about who you are or your family?

Guiding question
How do the pictures show us more about Grace, Mr Milligan, and their emotions or culture?

During reading-
Check pause points

After reading-
Guiding question
How do the pictures show us more about Grace, Mr Milligan, and their emotions or culture?
Anticipated responses: 
The colours change to show emotions. There are bright colours for happy moments and darker colours when Charlie dies.
The characters’ body language shows feelings, like Mr Milligan slumping when he’s grieving, and Grace holding her head in her hands.
Grace’s necklace and drawings give clues about her culture, showing symbols that appear again in her artwork even though the words never mention it.
The endpapers show important memories, with a photo wall showing Grace, Charlie, and Mr Milligan together, highlighting what Mr Milligan treasures.
